title: Instance Fields and Instance Methods
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of instance fields and instance methods and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—object-specific state—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study instance fields and instance methods with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you model valid object state and expose behavior without leaking implementation details. In this lesson, focus on object-specific state and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.
